recipe_navigation.name: 1.1 Retrieving All Rows and Columns from a Table
recipe_navigation.intent: Inspect the contents of an unfamiliar table.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Select the whole rowset for exploration; replace the wildcard with an explicit projection when creating a stable interface.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One row per stored record.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Compare returned column names and types with the consuming report contract.

recipe_navigation.name: 1.2 Retrieving a Subset of Rows from a Table
recipe_navigation.intent: Keep records satisfying a single condition.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Apply the population condition in WHERE before returning the selected columns.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One row per qualifying source record.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test one included row, one excluded row, and a NULL predicate input.

recipe_navigation.name: 1.3 Finding Rows That Satisfy Multiple Conditions
recipe_navigation.intent: Combine several inclusion and exclusion conditions.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Group AND and OR clauses with parentheses matching the intended alternatives.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One row per source record that passes the combined predicate.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Construct a small truth table containing one case for each alternative and overlap.

recipe_navigation.name: 1.4 Retrieving a Subset of Columns from a Table
recipe_navigation.intent: Return only fields needed by the next consumer.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: List required columns in SELECT instead of relying on a wildcard.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One output row per input row retained by any filters.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Verify required identifier columns were not removed and column order is documented.

recipe_navigation.name: 1.5 Providing Meaningful Names for Columns
recipe_navigation.intent: Make query output labels understandable.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Alias selected expressions with meaningful result-column names.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: Detail grain unchanged by renaming.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Check aliases for uniqueness and agreement with downstream field references.

recipe_navigation.name: 1.6 Referencing an Aliased Column in the WHERE Clause
recipe_navigation.intent: Filter a computed or renamed column that is not visible to the same SELECT-level WHERE.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Put the expression in an inline view and filter its output alias in an outer query.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: Inner detail or computed row grain; outer query retains qualifying inner rows.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Compare outer-alias filtering with the intended expression and test NULL results.

recipe_navigation.name: 1.7 Concatenating Column Values
recipe_navigation.intent: Combine fields into a single display string.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Concatenate column expressions and separator literals using the selected database dialect.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One constructed string per source row.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test NULL components, numeric casts, empty strings, and the separator placement.

recipe_navigation.name: 1.8 Using Conditional Logic in a SELECT Statement
recipe_navigation.intent: Assign an output value according to row-level conditions.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Use ordered CASE branches and an explicit ELSE when unmatched rows need a defined outcome.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One classification per source row.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test both sides of every threshold and a value that reaches ELSE.

recipe_navigation.name: 1.9 Limiting the Number of Rows Returned
recipe_navigation.intent: Return a bounded sample where any rows are acceptable.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Apply the source-era row-limiting mechanism for the selected dialect.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: At most n source rows.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Check n=0, fewer than n available rows, and whether the real task needs ordered rather than arbitrary selection.

recipe_navigation.name: 1.10 Returning n Random Records from a Table
recipe_navigation.intent: Take a randomly selected set of rows.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Order by a database random-value expression, then apply the row cap.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: At most n randomly ordered source rows.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Repeat the query and check the sample size, population filters, and whether reproducibility is required.

recipe_navigation.name: 1.11 Finding Null Values
recipe_navigation.intent: Find missing values explicitly.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Use IS NULL rather than equality to NULL.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One row per source record with a NULL in the tested column.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test NULL, zero, and an empty string as distinct inputs subject to the target dialect.

recipe_navigation.name: 1.12 Transforming Nulls into Real Values
recipe_navigation.intent: Show a replacement when a selected value is missing.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Use COALESCE to select the first non-NULL expression.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: Detail grain retained.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Verify that replacing missing with zero or text is justified and that types are compatible.

recipe_navigation.name: 1.13 Searching for Patterns
recipe_navigation.intent: Search strings using a wildcard pattern.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Apply LIKE with percent for variable-length text and underscore for a single character.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One row per matching source record.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Include positive, negative, literal-wildcard, and case-variant examples.

recipe_navigation.name: 2.1 Returning Query Results in a Specified Order
recipe_navigation.intent: Display rows in a specified value order.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Use ORDER BY with an explicit direction for the selected sort expression.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: Detail grain unchanged.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Include ties and decide whether a unique final tie-breaker is needed.

recipe_navigation.name: 2.2 Sorting by Multiple Fields
recipe_navigation.intent: Sort by one criterion within another.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: List sort keys in precedence order, with a direction on each key.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: Detail grain unchanged.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test tied primary keys, mixed directions, and changes to the SELECT list.

recipe_navigation.name: 2.3 Sorting by Substrings
recipe_navigation.intent: Order records by part of a string.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Extract the relevant substring in the sorting expression.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: Detail grain unchanged.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Use short strings and boundary positions to catch off-by-one extraction errors.

recipe_navigation.name: 2.4 Sorting Mixed Alphanumeric Data
recipe_navigation.intent: Sort mixed text and digits by the desired component.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Isolate the relevant component with character translation and replacement, then sort on it.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One derived sorting component per input row.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test values containing 2 and 10, no digits, multiple numeric runs, and padding.

recipe_navigation.name: 2.5 Dealing with Nulls When Sorting
recipe_navigation.intent: Control where NULLs appear without reversing non-NULL values.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Sort first on a CASE-derived missingness flag and then on the actual value, or use a source-documented NULL placement clause.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: Detail grain unchanged.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test both sort directions with NULL, zero, and tied non-NULL values.

recipe_navigation.name: 2.6 Sorting on a Data-Dependent Key
recipe_navigation.intent: Choose a sorting field according to each row’s type.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Return the appropriate sort value from CASE inside ORDER BY.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One chosen sort key per detail record.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Check each CASE branch, compatible return types, and ties across branches.

recipe_navigation.name: 3.1 Stacking One Rowset atop Another
recipe_navigation.intent: Stack compatible rowsets without joining their entities.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Align projected columns and combine rowsets with UNION ALL; use UNION only when set-level duplicate removal is intended.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One output occurrence per contributing input occurrence with UNION ALL.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Check projection order, compatible types, expected row-count sum, and duplicate policy.

recipe_navigation.name: 3.2 Combining Related Rows
recipe_navigation.intent: Attach attributes from a related entity.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Join using the established matching columns, separating relationship conditions from population filters.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: Source example: employee rows related to their department.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Check department-key uniqueness, employee match counts, and unmatched employees.

recipe_navigation.name: 3.3 Finding Rows in Common Between Two Tables
recipe_navigation.intent: Find rows shared across two sources using a complete comparison definition.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Join on every comparison column or use a compatible set intersection when only shared values are needed.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One comparison tuple or intended matched entity.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Create rows equal on one field but different on another; also test duplicate tuples and NULLs.

recipe_navigation.name: 3.4 Retrieving Values from One Table That Do Not Exist in Another
recipe_navigation.intent: Find values present in the first source and absent from the second.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Use set difference or a NULL-reviewed anti-membership test.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One returned comparison value under set semantics, or retained source occurrences under a predicate.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test an empty target, a target NULL, duplicate source values, and a NULL source key.

recipe_navigation.name: 3.5 Retrieving Rows from One Table That Do Not Correspond to Rows in Another
recipe_navigation.intent: Return full source rows lacking a corresponding related row.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Preserve the source with a left join and keep rows where a reliable target match column is NULL.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One row per unmatched source entity.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Verify the tested target column cannot be NULL on a genuine match; compare with a correlated absence test.

recipe_navigation.name: 3.6 Adding Joins to a Query Without Interfering with Other Joins
recipe_navigation.intent: Add optional information without losing previously returned records.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Use an outer join for optional related rows, or a scalar subquery only when at most one related value is guaranteed.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: Original result grain unless multiple optional matches expand it.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Compare source-key counts before and after, including zero, one, and two optional matches.

recipe_navigation.name: 3.7 Determining Whether Two Tables Have the Same Data
recipe_navigation.intent: Determine whether two rowsets contain the same data and multiplicities.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Compare both directions, including grouped occurrence counts where duplicates matter, and combine discrepancies.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: Comparison tuple plus occurrence count when evaluating bags.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test equal counts with different values and equal distinct values with different repetition counts.

recipe_navigation.name: 3.8 Identifying and Avoiding Cartesian Products
recipe_navigation.intent: Diagnose a join that creates unrelated combinations.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Inspect the relationship graph and add the missing relationship predicates; retain a cross join only when every combination is intended.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: Either a justified pair of input rows or the intended related entity.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Predict the product size before joining and examine repeated keys afterward.

recipe_navigation.name: 3.9 Performing Joins When Using Aggregates
recipe_navigation.intent: Avoid counting a parent measure multiple times after a detail join.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Aggregate the parent measure at its own grain before joining; the book’s DISTINCT-aggregate shortcut is conditional on value uniqueness.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: Employee salary grain versus employee-bonus row grain, then requested department summary.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Add two employees with equal salaries and one employee with multiple bonuses; reconcile against independent source totals.

recipe_navigation.name: 3.10 Performing Outer Joins When Using Aggregates
recipe_navigation.intent: Include parents without detail while computing correct totals.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Preserve the required parent population with an outer join and protect parent-grain aggregates from detail duplication.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: All qualifying employees, with bonus detail aggregated appropriately.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test a department with no bonuses, repeated bonuses, and two equal salaries.

recipe_navigation.name: 3.11 Returning Missing Data from Multiple Tables
recipe_navigation.intent: Show matched records and unmatched records from either side.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Use a supported full outer join or the source’s combination of opposite outer joins.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: Matched pairs plus unmatched source entities.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test left-only, right-only, one-to-many, and duplicate-identical matched rows.

recipe_navigation.name: 3.12 Using NULLs in Operations and Comparisons
recipe_navigation.intent: Compare or calculate with missing values when an explicit replacement is intended.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Replace missing values with COALESCE before the comparison or expression only when that substitution matches the question.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One comparison or expression result per source row.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Contrast results under missing-as-zero and missing-excluded interpretations.

recipe_navigation.name: 4.1 Inserting a New Record
recipe_navigation.intent: Insert a new row with a clear column-to-value mapping.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Provide an explicit target column list and compatible VALUES expressions.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One new target row per supplied values tuple.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Preview each value against its target type and required constraints; verify affected-row count.

recipe_navigation.name: 4.2 Inserting Default Values
recipe_navigation.intent: Create rows using column defaults.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Omit defaulted columns or use the source-supported DEFAULT form for the dialect.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One inserted row per insertion operation or tuple.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Inspect actual default expressions and test mixed defaulted/nondefaulted columns.

recipe_navigation.name: 4.3 Overriding a Default Value with NULL
recipe_navigation.intent: Store NULL instead of accepting a default.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Include the nullable target column and supply NULL explicitly.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One target row per insert tuple.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Check that the column permits NULL and compare omitted-column versus explicit-NULL inserts in a safe test.

recipe_navigation.name: 4.4 Copying Rows from One Table into Another
recipe_navigation.intent: Copy qualifying rows into another table.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Use INSERT with a SELECT whose projected columns align with the target column list.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One target row per selected input row unless constraints reject the operation.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Run the SELECT first; compare types, row count, duplicate keys, and restart behavior.

recipe_navigation.name: 4.5 Copying a Table Definition
recipe_navigation.intent: Create an empty table patterned on another row shape.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Use the source dialect’s LIKE, CTAS with a false predicate, or SELECT INTO form.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: Schema operation; no source rows should be copied.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Verify zero rows and inspect resulting types, defaults, indexes, and constraints instead of assuming a complete clone.

recipe_navigation.name: 4.6 Inserting into Multiple Tables at Once
recipe_navigation.intent: Route selected rows into multiple targets.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Use the source’s Oracle multitable insert or constrained DB2 union-view approach.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One selected row may map to one or multiple target rows according to routing semantics.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test overlapping routes, unmatched routes, and DB2 constraint exclusivity.

recipe_navigation.name: 4.7 Blocking Inserts to Certain Columns
recipe_navigation.intent: Limit which columns an insert interface exposes.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Expose permitted columns through an insertable view and restrict direct base-table insertion permissions.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One insertion through the approved view interface.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Review privileges and view insertability; test omitted mandatory columns.

recipe_navigation.name: 4.8 Modifying Records in a Table
recipe_navigation.intent: Update a defined population using an expression.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Put the replacement expression in SET and the intended target population in the outer WHERE.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One modification per qualifying target row.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Preview old and proposed values with SELECT and verify the intended affected keys.

recipe_navigation.name: 4.9 Updating When Corresponding Rows Exist
recipe_navigation.intent: Update only rows that have a qualifying related record.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Use a matching subquery with IN or EXISTS to constrain the target population.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One qualifying target row, independent of the number of existence matches.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test no match, one match, and multiple matches; ensure nonmatching rows remain unchanged.

recipe_navigation.name: 4.10 Updating with Values from Another Table
recipe_navigation.intent: Update values from a related source without overwriting unrelated targets.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Join to a unique source value or use a correlated value subquery plus an outer target-existence filter.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One source value per intended target row.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test an unmatched target and duplicate source matches; preview new values and affected keys.

recipe_navigation.name: 4.11 Merging Records
recipe_navigation.intent: Apply different changes to matched and unmatched target records.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Express matching, update/insert, and any deletion eligibility as separate branches of the intended merge operation.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One intended source-to-target match decision per entity.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test each action branch, multiple source matches, and idempotent reruns before any live write.

recipe_navigation.name: 4.12 Deleting All Records from a Table
recipe_navigation.intent: Remove every row from a table deliberately.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Use an unfiltered DELETE only for an explicitly approved all-row removal.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: All rows of the chosen table.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Confirm table identity, affected-row expectation, dependencies, and rollback capability before execution.

recipe_navigation.name: 4.13 Deleting Specific Records
recipe_navigation.intent: Delete a selected subset of records.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Use DELETE with the exact population predicate already reviewed as a SELECT.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One deletion per qualifying target row.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Review selected identifiers and counts before the write; include near-miss rows in the test.

recipe_navigation.name: 4.14 Deleting a Single Record
recipe_navigation.intent: Delete a single known record.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Filter by an inspected primary or unique key rather than an ambiguous attribute.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One specifically identified target entity.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Confirm exactly one previewed record and distinguish missing-key from multiple-match errors.

recipe_navigation.name: 4.15 Deleting Referential Integrity Violations
recipe_navigation.intent: Identify and remove orphaned child records after explicit review.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Find child rows whose parent cannot be found using a correlated absence predicate.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One candidate orphan child row.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Validate parent completeness and NULL-key policy before deleting; do not equate a late parent export with an invalid child.

recipe_navigation.name: 4.16 Deleting Duplicate Records
recipe_navigation.intent: Remove redundant rows under a defined duplicate rule.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Group by the duplicate-defining fields, choose one retained unique identifier, and delete only the other identifiers.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One survivor per defined duplicate group.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Preview groups and retained IDs, confirm tie-breaking policy, and reconcile kept plus deleted counts.

recipe_navigation.name: 4.17 Deleting Records Referenced from Another Table
recipe_navigation.intent: Delete rows based on grouped evidence in another source.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Aggregate related events, filter qualifying groups with HAVING, then constrain deletion to those group keys.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: Event grain inside the subquery; target-record grain for deletion.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Check threshold boundaries and duplicate events before previewing target deletions.

recipe_navigation.name: 5.1 Listing Tables in a Schema
recipe_navigation.intent: Discover tables visible within a schema.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Query the dialect’s table metadata with an explicit schema or owner filter.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One metadata row per discovered table according to catalog semantics.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Compare known accessible objects with results; check schema casing and user permissions.

recipe_navigation.name: 5.2 Listing a Table’s Columns
recipe_navigation.intent: Discover columns and their declared types.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Read the selected table’s column metadata from the dialect’s catalog.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One metadata row per table column.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Verify schema qualification, ordinal order, nullability, and the meaning of reported type fields.

recipe_navigation.name: 5.3 Listing Indexed Columns for a Table
recipe_navigation.intent: Inspect indexed columns before making performance hypotheses.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Join or inspect index metadata using the database-specific catalog relationships.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: Index-column metadata, with index identity and column position retained.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Check composite order, duplicate index names across schemas, and actual execution plans.

recipe_navigation.name: 5.4 Listing Constraints on a Table
recipe_navigation.intent: Discover declared constraints and their participating columns.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Read constraint and key-column metadata with complete catalog identifiers.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One constraint-column association.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Verify multi-column constraints and join catalog rows by full constraint identity.

recipe_navigation.name: 5.5 Listing Foreign Keys Without Corresponding Indexes
recipe_navigation.intent: Find foreign-key columns lacking corresponding index evidence.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Compare foreign-key metadata with index-column metadata using an outer-join absence test.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: Foreign-key column or full composite constraint, depending on the audit.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Check full composite ordering, permissions, and the database’s definition of useful index coverage.

recipe_navigation.name: 5.6 Using SQL to Generate SQL
recipe_navigation.intent: Generate maintenance statement text from metadata or data.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Build statement strings with properly formatted values and object names, then inspect them before any separate execution.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One proposed statement per selected object or row.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Verify quoting, object identity, permissions, and a read-only preview of the affected population.

recipe_navigation.name: 5.7 Describing the Data Dictionary Views in an Oracle Database
recipe_navigation.intent: Discover what Oracle dictionary views describe.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Query DICTIONARY for view purposes and DICT_COLUMNS for their columns.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One dictionary view or dictionary column.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Check exact view names and privileges; distinguish descriptive comments from enforced constraints.

recipe_navigation.name: 6.1 Walking a String
recipe_navigation.intent: Turn a string into ordered character rows.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Pair each source string with enough integer positions, restrict positions to its length, and extract one character per position.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One source-string identity and character position.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test a string longer than the helper rowset, a trailing space, an empty value, and repeated characters.

recipe_navigation.name: 6.2 Embedding Quotes Within String Literals
recipe_navigation.intent: Represent quotation marks inside a SQL string literal.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Escape an embedded quote using the source’s doubled-quote literal pattern.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One constructed literal value.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test apostrophes, a quote-only value, an empty string, and NULL separately.

recipe_navigation.name: 6.3 Counting the Occurrences of a Character in a String
recipe_navigation.intent: Count occurrences of a delimiter or substring.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Compare the original length with the length after replacement and divide by the search-token length when needed.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One count per source string.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test no matches, repeated tokens, multicharacter tokens, overlaps, and an empty search token.

recipe_navigation.name: 6.4 Removing Unwanted Characters from a String
recipe_navigation.intent: Remove a defined set of unwanted characters.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Map a set of unwanted characters to a shared marker with TRANSLATE, then remove it with REPLACE, or use repeated REPLACE where shown.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One cleaned value per source row.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test a legitimate marker character, all-unwanted text, case variants, and preservation of allowed text.

recipe_navigation.name: 6.5 Separating Numeric and Character Data
recipe_navigation.intent: Separate digit and nondigit portions of mixed text.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Use character translation and replacement to isolate the two classes independently.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One pair of extracted components per source string.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test interleaved numeric runs, signs, decimals, spaces, and values containing only one class.

recipe_navigation.name: 6.6 Determining Whether a String Is Alphanumeric
recipe_navigation.intent: Identify strings consisting entirely of an allowed alphanumeric set.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Normalize allowed characters and detect anything remaining outside the permitted class, or use the source’s regex alternative.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One validity decision per source string.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Include punctuation, padding, accented letters, digits only, and letters only.

recipe_navigation.name: 6.7 Extracting Initials from a Name
recipe_navigation.intent: Extract initials under a limited name-format assumption.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Use the source’s delimiter and capitalization patterns to isolate initials from supported two- or three-part names.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One source name with documented component structure.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test middle initials, extra spaces, particles, lowercase names, and names outside the assumed format.

recipe_navigation.name: 6.8 Ordering by Parts of a String
recipe_navigation.intent: Sort on a portion of a string without changing its display.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Place the substring expression in ORDER BY.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: Source detail grain.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Validate substring boundaries and provide a tie-breaker where order must be stable.

recipe_navigation.name: 6.9 Ordering by a Number in a String
recipe_navigation.intent: Order mixed strings by an embedded numeric value.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Remove nondigits using the source’s character operations and use the extracted numeric portion as the sort criterion.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One extracted sort component per source row.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test numeric 2 versus 10, multiple numeric runs, no digits, and values outside the target numeric range.

recipe_navigation.name: 6.10 Creating a Delimited List from Table Rows
recipe_navigation.intent: Build a delimited list from rows in each group.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Group the source values and concatenate them in a specified within-group order using a dialect-appropriate mechanism.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One list per group.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test duplicate values, NULL members, embedded delimiters, length limits, and repeatable ordering.

recipe_navigation.name: 6.11 Converting Delimited Data into a Multivalued IN-List
recipe_navigation.intent: Use serialized values as a membership rowset.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Split the delimited input into typed value rows before using it in an IN predicate.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One parsed token, then qualifying source detail rows.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test spaces, empty tokens, duplicate tokens, invalid casts, quoted delimiters, and helper-position capacity.

recipe_navigation.name: 6.12 Alphabetizing a String
recipe_navigation.intent: Alphabetize the characters within each string.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Expand to character rows, order characters within the original string identity, and reassemble.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: Source-string identity plus character position, reduced back to one string.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Check that output character counts and multiplicities equal input counts; test duplicate source strings separately.

recipe_navigation.name: 6.13 Identifying Strings That Can Be Treated as Numbers
recipe_navigation.intent: Find numeric content in mixed strings under the recipe’s extraction rule.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Identify digit-bearing strings, isolate their digits, and cast only the resulting component.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One digit-bearing source row and its extracted numeric component.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test letters around digits, multiple runs, signs, decimals, no digits, and overflow.

recipe_navigation.name: 6.14 Extracting the nth Delimited Substring
recipe_navigation.intent: Retrieve a particular token from each delimited string.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Preserve original row identity and token ordinal during splitting, then select the requested position.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: Original row identity plus token ordinal.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test repeated tokens, two separate source rows, missing nth tokens, and consecutive delimiters.

recipe_navigation.name: 6.15 Parsing an IP Address
recipe_navigation.intent: Break a dotted IP-style string into components.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Locate delimiter boundaries and extract each component, using split functions or recursive substring processing as shown.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One component position per original dotted string.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Check exactly four intended components, empty pieces, extra delimiters, and numeric range separately.

recipe_navigation.name: 6.16 Comparing Strings by Sound
recipe_navigation.intent: Find candidate text matches based on similar sound.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Compare SOUNDEX encodings, using a self-join when candidates come from the same source.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: A candidate pair of source strings.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Review false matches, language assumptions, self-pairs, and reversed duplicate pairs.

recipe_navigation.name: 6.17 Finding Text Not Matching a Pattern
recipe_navigation.intent: Find apparent structured values whose formatting is invalid.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Define a broad candidate pattern, remove correctly formatted instances, and check whether candidate-like material remains.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One text row containing candidate structured values.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test no candidate, valid only, invalid only, and mixed valid/invalid instances in one comment.

recipe_navigation.name: 7.1 Computing an Average
recipe_navigation.intent: Compute an average over the intended population.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Use AVG over the qualifying rowset, with GROUP BY when a separate result is required per group.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One overall or group-level aggregate.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Compare sum and contributing count; include NULL and empty-group cases.

recipe_navigation.name: 7.2 Finding the Min/Max Value in a Column
recipe_navigation.intent: Find extreme values in a population.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Use MIN and MAX over the intended rowset or grouping.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One extreme-value pair per group or population.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test tied extrema, all-NULL groups, and a single-row group.

recipe_navigation.name: 7.3 Summing the Values in a Column
recipe_navigation.intent: Add the values belonging to a defined population.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Use SUM at the requested grouping grain.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One sum per defined group.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Reconcile group totals to an independently computed population total; test duplicates introduced by joins.

recipe_navigation.name: 7.4 Counting Rows in a Table
recipe_navigation.intent: Count rows rather than values in one field.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Use COUNT(*) over the rowset or grouped rowset.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One count per group or whole input.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Compare the count before and after every join and distinguish source rows from NULL-extended rows.

recipe_navigation.name: 7.5 Counting Values in a Column
recipe_navigation.intent: Count populated values in a particular column.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Use COUNT(column) when the question is how many rows have a non-NULL value in that expression.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One populated-value count per group.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Compare COUNT(*) and COUNT(column); account for their difference using an explicit missingness count.

recipe_navigation.name: 7.6 Generating a Running Total
recipe_navigation.intent: Show a cumulative sum along an ordered sequence.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Apply SUM as an ordered window and establish a tie-breaker that matches the intended progression.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One original detail row with a cumulative measure.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Hand-check tied values, the first row, the final total, and partition resets.

recipe_navigation.name: 7.7 Generating a Running Product
recipe_navigation.intent: Compute a cumulative product for positive values.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Sum logarithms in an ordered window and exponentiate the result.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One cumulative result per ordered input row.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Compare against direct multiplication on a small fixture; test zero, negatives, NULL, and overflow.

recipe_navigation.name: 7.8 Smoothing a Series of Values
recipe_navigation.intent: Smooth a sequence using current and preceding observations.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Use LAG to align prior observations with the current row, then apply a stated moving-average expression.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One ordered observation with its selected predecessors.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Hand-check the first two rows, duplicate dates, missing dates, and numeric division.

recipe_navigation.name: 7.9 Calculating a Mode
recipe_navigation.intent: Find the most frequently occurring value.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Count occurrences by value and rank those counts, retaining all top ties when all modes are requested.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One frequency row per candidate value, then the highest-frequency candidates.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test two equally frequent modes and a population where all frequencies tie.

recipe_navigation.name: 7.10 Calculating a Median
recipe_navigation.intent: Find the median of a defined numeric population.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Use the source-described middle-value/50th-percentile concept with a verified median or percentile implementation.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One median per population or group; some window forms repeat it on detail rows.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Check [1,2,100], an even-sized set, tied values, all-equal values, and NULLs against hand-calculated medians.

recipe_navigation.name: 7.11 Determining the Percentage of a Total
recipe_navigation.intent: Compute a subset’s share of a broader total.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Calculate numerator and denominator over their explicitly defined populations before division.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One percentage per selected subset or reporting group.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Expose numerator and denominator separately; test a zero denominator and integer-typed inputs.

recipe_navigation.name: 7.12 Aggregating Nullable Columns
recipe_navigation.intent: Average a nullable measure under a deliberate missing-as-zero interpretation.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Apply COALESCE before AVG only when every population member should be represented in the denominator.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One average per defined population or group.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Compute both raw and zero-filled averages and explain which denominator answers the question.

recipe_navigation.name: 7.13 Computing Averages Without High and Low Values
recipe_navigation.intent: Compute an average after excluding extremes.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Identify minimum and maximum values, then exclude them under the chosen all-ties or single-observation rule.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One trimmed population per requested group.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test repeated extrema, all-equal values, and fewer than three observations.

recipe_navigation.name: 7.14 Converting Alphanumeric Strings into Numbers
recipe_navigation.intent: Extract digits from alphanumeric text before numeric use.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Translate or remove nondigits, then convert the retained digit sequence under the source’s assumptions.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One extracted digit sequence per input row.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test two separated numeric runs, decimals, signs, and no digits before adopting the extraction policy.

recipe_navigation.name: 7.15 Changing Values in a Running Total
recipe_navigation.intent: Accumulate additions and deductions in one running balance.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Map transaction categories to signed contributions with CASE, then compute an ordered window sum.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One ordered transaction per balance stream.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test both transaction directions, unknown categories, same-time events, and the opening-balance convention.

recipe_navigation.name: 7.16 Finding Outliers Using the Median Absolute Deviation
recipe_navigation.intent: Measure deviations from a robust central value.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Follow the source prose: compute the median, each absolute deviation from it, and the median of those deviations in stages.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One center/spread per population, then optional row-level deviation diagnostics.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Use [1,2,3] to distinguish centering on median from centering on MAD; also test zero MAD, ties, and missing values.

recipe_navigation.name: 7.17 Finding Anomalies Using Benford’s Law
recipe_navigation.intent: Compare observed first-digit frequencies with a reference distribution.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Build observed digit counts and an expected-digit rowset, then preserve expected digits even when observations are absent.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One first-digit category from 1 through 9.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Check absent digits yield zero observed count, all shares use the eligible denominator, and excluded zero/negative/decimal inputs are accounted for.

recipe_navigation.name: 8.1 Adding and Subtracting Days, Months, and Years
recipe_navigation.intent: Shift a date by a named interval.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Add or subtract a specified number of days, months, or years using the dialect’s date or interval expressions.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One shifted date per source date and requested offset.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test month-end dates, leap day, negative offsets, and timestamp precision.

recipe_navigation.name: 8.2 Determining the Number of Days Between Two Dates
recipe_navigation.intent: Measure the day difference between two selected dates.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Resolve each endpoint to one row, then apply the dialect’s subtraction or day-difference function.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One endpoint pair.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Swap endpoints to check sign, test equal dates, and verify each endpoint query returns one row.

recipe_navigation.name: 8.3 Determining the Number of Business Days Between Two Dates
recipe_navigation.intent: Count working days across an inclusive date interval.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Generate every date in the interval, remove the excluded weekdays, and count the remainder; a supplied holiday rowset may further exclude dates.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One generated calendar date between the two included endpoints.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test same-day intervals, weekend endpoints, holidays, reversed bounds, and generator capacity.

recipe_navigation.name: 8.4 Determining the Number of Months or Years Between Two Dates
recipe_navigation.intent: Express the separation of two dates in months or years.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Compute year/month component differences or a source-provided month-difference function, then use an explicitly chosen year-conversion rule.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One date pair.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test same-month dates, partial years, month ends, and the intended rounding behavior.

recipe_navigation.name: 8.5 Determining the Number of Seconds, Minutes, or Hours Between Two Dates
recipe_navigation.intent: Express a date difference in smaller time units.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Use a supported unit-aware difference or convert the source’s day difference to hours, minutes, or seconds.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One pair of temporal values.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test a sub-day interval, fractional seconds, overflow, and a zone-transition case when applicable.

recipe_navigation.name: 8.6 Counting the Occurrences of Weekdays in a Year
recipe_navigation.intent: Count each weekday within a year.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Generate all dates from the year’s start to the next year’s boundary, derive weekday values, and group them.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One date in the selected year, then one aggregate per weekday.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Ensure counts sum to the year’s date count and test leap and non-leap years.

recipe_navigation.name: 8.7 Determining the Date Difference Between the Current Record and the Next Record
recipe_navigation.intent: Compare a date to the next relevant date in its sequence.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Find the following date with LEAD or the source’s correlated next-date query, then compute the interval.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One source row within its ordered population.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test tied dates, the final row, different partitions, and a stable secondary ordering key.

recipe_navigation.name: 9.1 Determining Whether a Year Is a Leap Year
recipe_navigation.intent: Determine whether a specified year contains leap day.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Use the source’s date construction and February-end logic to inspect the year’s calendar.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One selected calendar year.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test years divisible by 100 and 400 as well as ordinary leap and common years.

recipe_navigation.name: 9.2 Determining the Number of Days in a Year
recipe_navigation.intent: Count the days in a year.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Derive the year boundaries and calculate their separation, or use the source’s final-day-of-year method.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One calendar year.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Check a leap year and a common year; compare with an enumerated calendar count.

recipe_navigation.name: 9.3 Extracting Units of Time from a Date
recipe_navigation.intent: Extract selected units from a date.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Use the dialect’s extraction or formatting functions for the needed date components.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One component tuple per source date.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Confirm return types, weekday numbering, and whether year is needed to disambiguate a grouped month.

recipe_navigation.name: 9.4 Determining the First and Last Days of a Month
recipe_navigation.intent: Find the month boundaries containing a date.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Normalize to month start and derive month end using the next month or a supplied last-day function.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One calendar month associated with each input date.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test February, leap day, year-end, and source timestamps with a nonmidnight time.

recipe_navigation.name: 9.5 Determining All Dates for a Particular Weekday Throughout a Year
recipe_navigation.intent: List every occurrence of a given weekday in a year.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Generate the year’s dates and filter by the chosen weekday, or advance from an initial matching day as shown.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One matching calendar date.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Verify every result has the required weekday and lies inside the requested year.

recipe_navigation.name: 9.6 Determining the Date of the First and Last Occurrences of a Specific Weekday in a Month
recipe_navigation.intent: Find the first and last occurrence of a weekday in a month.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Anchor the search on month boundaries and select the earliest/latest date matching the required weekday.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One chosen weekday within one calendar month.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test a month whose first or last day already matches the weekday.

recipe_navigation.name: 9.7 Creating a Calendar
recipe_navigation.intent: Display a calendar-shaped result from dates.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Generate dates, derive week and weekday positions, and pivot day numbers into weekday columns.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: Calendar dates transformed into one output row per displayed week.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test a month spanning year-end, a month starting midweek, and blank cells outside the month.

recipe_navigation.name: 9.8 Listing Quarter Start and End Dates for the Year
recipe_navigation.intent: List the four quarter intervals of a calendar year.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Generate four quarter ordinals and convert them to three-month start/end boundaries.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One row per calendar quarter.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Check contiguous coverage, quarter 4 crossing to the next year, and exactly four results.

recipe_navigation.name: 9.9 Determining Quarter Start and End Dates for a Given Quarter
recipe_navigation.intent: Decode a year-quarter identifier into boundaries.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Separate the year from the quarter component and construct its starting and ending months.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One validated year-quarter code.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Reject quarter values outside 1–4, malformed years, and padded or NULL codes.

recipe_navigation.name: 9.10 Filling in Missing Dates
recipe_navigation.intent: Show periods even when no facts occurred.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Generate the complete period rowset, then outer join facts at matching period grain and aggregate matched records.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One generated period, with facts assigned to the same period key.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Check generator endpoints, one period per key, and a known no-activity month; compare COUNT(*) with a fact-key count.

recipe_navigation.name: 9.11 Searching on Specific Units of Time
recipe_navigation.intent: Search by a date component rather than a complete date.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Extract the specific month, weekday, or other requested unit and apply the component predicate.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One source record whose date component qualifies.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test the same month across different years and localized day names.

recipe_navigation.name: 9.12 Comparing Records Using Specific Parts of a Date
recipe_navigation.intent: Compare records by selected parts of their dates.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Self-join candidate records and compare the extracted month/weekday components while excluding unwanted self-pairs.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: A qualifying pair of distinct source records.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Check self-pairs, reversed duplicates, different years, and multiple records sharing the same date.

recipe_navigation.name: 9.13 Identifying Overlapping Date Ranges
recipe_navigation.intent: Find overlapping project intervals for the same entity.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Self-join intervals within the entity and identify starts that fall inside another interval under the source’s inclusive boundary rule.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: A pair of distinct intervals belonging to the same entity.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test disjoint, touching, nested, identical-start, reversed, and open-ended intervals; avoid duplicate pair counting.

recipe_navigation.name: 10.1 Locating a Range of Consecutive Values
recipe_navigation.intent: Find neighboring intervals that form a consecutive sequence.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Use LEAD to inspect the next interval’s boundary and compare it with the current interval’s end.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One interval and its immediate successor within the intended stream.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test one-row input, a gap, touching intervals, and order keys that do not follow chronology.

recipe_navigation.name: 10.2 Finding Differences Between Rows in the Same Group or Partition
recipe_navigation.intent: Compare successive values within a group.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Use a partitioned LEAD or LAG in a staged query, then subtract the aligned values.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One employee row within a department’s hire sequence.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test tied hire dates, one-row departments, and the last row of each group.

recipe_navigation.name: 10.3 Locating the Beginning and End of a Range of Consecutive Values
recipe_navigation.intent: Reduce consecutive interval runs to their beginning and end.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Mark breaks using the prior endpoint, accumulate the break flags into group identifiers, and aggregate each resulting run.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One ordered interval initially; one maximal consecutive run in the result.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test a singleton, several gaps, tied start times, and reconstruction of input intervals from run membership.

recipe_navigation.name: 10.4 Filling in Missing Values in a Range of Values
recipe_navigation.intent: Include missing numeric or year categories in a report.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Supply the complete category range and outer join facts before counting matched observations.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One generated category with zero or more matched facts.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Check range endpoints, category uniqueness, absent categories, and matching on the intended temporal key.

recipe_navigation.name: 10.5 Generating Consecutive Numeric Values
recipe_navigation.intent: Generate an integer rowset for controlled expansion.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Use a bounded recursive query, the source’s Oracle MODEL construction, or PostgreSQL GENERATE_SERIES as documented.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One row per integer in the defined sequence.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Verify row count, uniqueness, endpoints, termination, and the empty-range case.

recipe_navigation.name: 11.1 Paginating Through a Result Set
recipe_navigation.intent: Return a selected page of an ordered rowset.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Assign ROW_NUMBER under a defined ordering, then filter the numbered rows to the requested interval.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One source row with a deterministic ordinal.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Check adjacent pages for overlap/gaps, tied sort values, and changing source data between requests.

recipe_navigation.name: 11.2 Skipping n Rows from a Table
recipe_navigation.intent: Keep every nth row of a defined sequence.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Number the ordered rows and use modulo on that ordinal to select the required positions.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One source row and ordinal.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test the first included position, n=1, invalid n, and tied sort values.

recipe_navigation.name: 11.3 Incorporating OR Logic When Using Outer Joins
recipe_navigation.intent: Restrict optional matches while retaining the preserved outer population.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Move optional-side OR conditions into the join predicate or prefilter the optional rowset.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One preserved entity with qualifying optional matches.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test no match, a match failing the optional filter, and two eligible matches.

recipe_navigation.name: 11.4 Determining Which Rows Are Reciprocals
recipe_navigation.intent: Find reversed pairs such as (a,b) and (b,a).
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Self-join with the two comparison columns reversed and use a canonical pair ordering when only one representation is wanted.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One reciprocal value pair or source-row pair, as specified.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test equal values, duplicated source rows, missing reversed partners, and NULL components.

recipe_navigation.name: 11.5 Selecting the Top n Records
recipe_navigation.intent: Select top-ranked rows under an explicit tie policy.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Use DENSE_RANK for the top n distinct values or ROW_NUMBER for exactly n ranked positions.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: A ranked detail row within the relevant population.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test a tie at the cutoff and verify whether all tied records or exactly n rows are intended.

recipe_navigation.name: 11.6 Finding Records with the Highest and Lowest Values
recipe_navigation.intent: Return detail records owning minimum or maximum values.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Expose group or population MIN/MAX through window expressions, then filter the original rows against them.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One detail record with reference extrema.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test ties at each extreme, a single-row population, and all-NULL measures.

recipe_navigation.name: 11.7 Investigating Future Rows
recipe_navigation.intent: Identify records based on the next observation.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Define the sequence, expose the following value with LEAD, and compare it to the current value.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One current observation and its selected successor.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test tied timestamps, missing successors, and whether next means next row or next distinct time.

recipe_navigation.name: 11.8 Shifting Row Values
recipe_navigation.intent: Attach preceding and following values, optionally wrapping at the ends.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Use LAG and LEAD under the chosen order and supply the source-described endpoint fallback for a circular result.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One ordered detail row with adjacent values.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test one-row input, tied values, and first/last rows; distinguish a NULL neighbor from no neighbor.

recipe_navigation.name: 11.9 Ranking Results
recipe_navigation.intent: Assign rankings while deciding how ties should behave.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Choose DENSE_RANK, RANK, or ROW_NUMBER according to the requested tie and gap behavior.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One ranking result per detail row.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Use values with a tie followed by a new value and compare the resulting rank sequences.

recipe_navigation.name: 11.10 Suppressing Duplicates
recipe_navigation.intent: Return unique projected values deliberately.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Use DISTINCT or GROUP BY for a unique-value list, or partitioned ROW_NUMBER when selecting a defined representative row.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One row per desired distinct projection or representative group.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Check which columns define uniqueness and whether dropping multiplicity is intentional.

recipe_navigation.name: 11.11 Finding Knight Values
recipe_navigation.intent: Retrieve an attribute belonging to a row selected by a different ordering field.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Find the latest qualifying row per group and carry its associated attribute, using the source’s CASE/window or Oracle KEEP pattern.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One selected latest-row attribute per group, optionally repeated on details.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test tied latest dates, negative/zero attributes, and latest rows whose attribute is not the group maximum.

recipe_navigation.name: 11.12 Generating Simple Forecasts
recipe_navigation.intent: Expand an order into a small schedule of predefined future actions.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Cross join each order to a bounded stage-number rowset and derive action labels and dates with CASE.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One order-stage pair.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Verify the stage multiplier, action order, date offsets, and exactly one row per order-stage key.

recipe_navigation.name: 12.1 Pivoting a Result Set into One Row
recipe_navigation.intent: Turn grouped categories into columns in a single summary row.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Use one conditional aggregate per chosen category.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One overall summary or explicit reporting group.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Reconcile the wide columns to the original grouped totals; test absent and unexpected categories.

recipe_navigation.name: 12.2 Pivoting a Result Set into Multiple Rows
recipe_navigation.intent: Pivot multiple items per category without losing members.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Assign ROW_NUMBER within each category, then pivot while grouping by that within-category position.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One member per category and ordinal; one output row per ordinal.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test unequal category lengths, duplicate names, stable ordering, and total member preservation.

recipe_navigation.name: 12.3 Reverse Pivoting a Result Set
recipe_navigation.intent: Convert wide category columns into labeled rows.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Cross join to a bounded category selector and use CASE to emit the corresponding column value and category label.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: Original row identity plus unpivoted category.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Check expected expansion factor, labels, all category columns, and missing values.

recipe_navigation.name: 12.4 Reverse Pivoting a Result Set into One Column
recipe_navigation.intent: Display several fields as a single vertical column.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Expand each input row by a small selector rowset and map selector positions to field values.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: Original entity plus display-field ordinal.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Verify field sequence, casts, row-count multiplier, and separation between entities.

recipe_navigation.name: 12.5 Suppressing Repeating Values from a Result Set
recipe_navigation.intent: Hide repeated group labels in a human-facing report.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Compare the current label with the preceding label using LAG and suppress repeated display values.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: Detail rows kept in a defined display sequence.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Verify stable grouping order and retain an unsuppressed key for downstream processing.

recipe_navigation.name: 12.6 Pivoting a Result Set to Facilitate Inter-Row Calculations
recipe_navigation.intent: Place selected group totals side by side before comparing them.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Compute conditional aggregates in an inner stage, then calculate the cross-column differences in an outer stage.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One selected comparison group or complete summary.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Reconcile each component independently and test missing categories before interpreting a difference.

recipe_navigation.name: 12.7 Creating Buckets of Data, of a Fixed Size
recipe_navigation.intent: Assign a fixed number of rows to each bucket.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Order and number rows, divide the ordinal by the requested bucket capacity, and take a ceiling with appropriate numeric types.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One row with a capacity-based bucket identifier.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test exact multiples, a final partial bucket, n=1, and integer-division behavior.

recipe_navigation.name: 12.8 Creating a Predefined Number of Buckets
recipe_navigation.intent: Distribute rows among a predefined number of buckets.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Apply NTILE to a deliberately ordered rowset.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One ranked source row with a bucket identifier.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test fewer rows than buckets, uneven division, and ties spanning bucket boundaries.

recipe_navigation.name: 12.9 Creating Horizontal Histograms
recipe_navigation.intent: Represent group counts as horizontal text bars.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Aggregate group counts, then repeat a display character according to each count.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One count and bar per group.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Verify bar length against numeric count and decide how to handle very large groups.

recipe_navigation.name: 12.10 Creating Vertical Histograms
recipe_navigation.intent: Represent group counts as vertical text bars.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Assign within-group positions and pivot those positions into a character matrix.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One displayed height position across groups.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Count displayed markers per category and verify top/bottom orientation and blank cells.

recipe_navigation.name: 12.11 Returning Non-GROUP BY Columns
recipe_navigation.intent: Retain detailed attributes while selecting rows using group aggregates.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Use window aggregates to expose reference values, then filter the detail rows by those values.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One detail row with its relevant group extrema.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test two rows tied at an extreme and columns that differ between those rows.

recipe_navigation.name: 12.12 Calculating Simple Subtotals
recipe_navigation.intent: Add a grand total to grouped summaries.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Use the source’s ROLLUP form or explicit aggregate branches, and label the aggregate level reliably.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One category subtotal plus a grand-total row.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Verify grand total equals independently summed detail and distinguish source NULL categories from the generated total.

recipe_navigation.name: 12.13 Calculating Subtotals for All Possible Expression Combinations
recipe_navigation.intent: Produce subtotals for every requested combination of dimensions.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Use CUBE or separate aggregate branches matching each required grouping level.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One row per grouping combination and level.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Validate every grouping level independently; do not sum the mixed-level output as one fact table.

recipe_navigation.name: 12.14 Identifying Rows That Are Not Subtotals
recipe_navigation.intent: Identify which output rows are generated subtotals.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Use GROUPING indicators to mark dimensions rolled out of the current aggregate level.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One aggregate output row with level indicators.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Insert a genuine NULL dimension value and verify it is distinct from the all-dimensions total.

recipe_navigation.name: 12.15 Using Case Expressions to Flag Rows
recipe_navigation.intent: Encode categories as separate indicator columns.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Use a CASE expression per category to emit the chosen true/false representation.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One source row with several category indicators.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test an unexpected category, a NULL category, and whether exactly one flag is expected per row.

recipe_navigation.name: 12.16 Creating a Sparse Matrix
recipe_navigation.intent: Create a sparse report matrix from categorical values.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Map categories to output columns with CASE while retaining the source rows; add a deliberate grouping key only when densification is wanted.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One original row or declared display group.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Verify that densification does not merge distinct entities and that category counts remain reconcilable.

recipe_navigation.name: 12.17 Grouping Rows by Units of Time
recipe_navigation.intent: Summarize observations into short time intervals under the source’s sampling assumption.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: The source groups consecutive transaction identifiers into five-row buckets and aggregates their times and counts.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: A fixed row/identifier bucket in the source example.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test missing IDs, multiple rows per second, irregular timestamps, and whether five rows really represent five seconds.

recipe_navigation.name: 12.18 Performing Aggregations over Different Groups/Partitions Simultaneously
recipe_navigation.intent: Attach several differently grouped aggregates to each detail row.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Use multiple window expressions with different PARTITION BY definitions.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One detail record with several reference scopes.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Reconcile each partition’s value independently and verify the detail row count remains unchanged.

recipe_navigation.name: 12.19 Performing Aggregations over a Moving Range of Values
recipe_navigation.intent: Aggregate over a moving time/value range rather than a fixed row count.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Use a supported RANGE frame or a correlated range predicate matching the intended boundary interval.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One current observation with all contributing observations in its specified range.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test a value exactly on the lower boundary, tied dates, sparse dates, and an interval with no prior observations.

recipe_navigation.name: 12.20 Pivoting a Result Set with Subtotals
recipe_navigation.intent: Build a wide report while retaining reliable subtotal levels.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Generate the requested grouped totals first, retain GROUPING markers, and then pivot for presentation.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One declared subtotal level and reporting key before reshaping.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Reconcile each level before and after pivoting; test NULL categories and row ordering.

recipe_navigation.name: 13.1 Expressing a Parent-Child Relationship
recipe_navigation.intent: Attach the immediate parent’s information to each child.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Self-join the child’s parent-reference column to the parent row’s identity column.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One child-to-parent relationship.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test a root, an orphan reference, duplicate parent identifiers, and a normal child.

recipe_navigation.name: 13.2 Expressing a Child-Parent-Grandparent Relationship
recipe_navigation.intent: Traverse from a child toward its ancestors.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Anchor on the chosen child and repeatedly follow its parent reference using the source’s recursive or CONNECT BY form.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One visited ancestor step per starting child and path.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test a two-level tree, a deeper tree, a missing parent, and a cycle; verify the displayed path direction.

recipe_navigation.name: 13.3 Creating a Hierarchical View of a Table
recipe_navigation.intent: Build a hierarchy from its root downward.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Anchor on the root and recursively match child parent-references to the current node’s identity, accumulating a path if required.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One visited node per traversal path.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test multiple roots, disconnected rows, repeated paths, deep chains, and cycles.

recipe_navigation.name: 13.4 Finding All Child Rows for a Given Parent Row
recipe_navigation.intent: Find all descendants of a selected parent.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Start at the chosen parent and repeatedly expand matching children, retaining the anchor only when the requested result includes it.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One visited descendant entity or path.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test a parent with no children, several levels, duplicate paths, and a cycle; confirm anchor inclusion.

recipe_navigation.name: 13.5 Determining Which Rows Are Leaf, Branch, or Root Nodes
recipe_navigation.intent: Classify hierarchy rows as roots, branches, or leaves.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Combine the presence of a parent reference with evidence that other rows reference the current node.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One classification per node under the stated tree model.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test a standalone node, a root with children, an ordinary branch, an orphan, and self-reference.

recipe_navigation.name: 14.1 Creating Cross-Tab Reports Using SQL Server’s PIVOT Operator
recipe_navigation.intent: Use SQL Server’s native operator for a cross-tab.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Provide the intended aggregate measure, pivot category, and fixed output-category list to PIVOT.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One row per remaining nonpivot grouping key.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Inspect driver columns for unintended implicit grouping; reconcile totals to a nonpivot aggregate.

recipe_navigation.name: 14.2 Unpivoting a Cross-Tab Report Using SQL Server’s UNPIVOT Operator
recipe_navigation.intent: Use SQL Server’s native operator to turn columns into rows.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Select the intended wide columns and expose their names and values through UNPIVOT.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: Original row identity plus unpivoted column label.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Check all intended input columns, result types, expected expansion, and NULL-cell behavior.

recipe_navigation.name: 14.3 Transposing a Result Set Using Oracle’s MODEL Clause
recipe_navigation.intent: Express a transpose through Oracle’s MODEL clause.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Treat the rowset as model dimensions and measures and apply the source’s aggregate/CASE rules.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: Declared model dimension tuple.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Verify unique dimension coordinates, referenced cells, and totals against a simpler conditional aggregate.

recipe_navigation.name: 14.4 Extracting Elements of a String from Unfixed Locations
recipe_navigation.intent: Extract values enclosed by delimiters at variable positions.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Locate successive opening and closing brackets, then extract the text between each pair.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One source log string with the expected bracketed fields.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test missing/extra brackets, nested brackets, empty fields, and a changed number of components.

recipe_navigation.name: 14.5 Finding the Number of Days in a Year (an Alternate Solution for Oracle)
recipe_navigation.intent: Compute year length with Oracle-specific date formatting.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Derive the last day of the year and read its day-of-year value.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One calendar year.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Compare leap and common years and confirm the formatting result’s numeric conversion.

recipe_navigation.name: 14.6 Searching for Mixed Alphanumeric Strings
recipe_navigation.intent: Find strings containing both letters and digits.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Map letters and digits to distinguishable markers and require the presence of both classes.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One decision per input string.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test letters only, digits only, punctuation plus both classes, and non-ASCII text.

recipe_navigation.name: 14.7 Converting Whole Numbers to Binary Using Oracle
recipe_navigation.intent: Explore procedural-style iteration within Oracle SQL.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Use the source’s MODEL iteration to generate a binary representation from a whole number.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One nonnegative whole-number input and its model iteration state.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test zero, one, a power of two, a nearby value, negatives, and iteration limits.

recipe_navigation.name: 14.8 Pivoting a Ranked Result Set
recipe_navigation.intent: Display ranked groups in separate report columns.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Rank values with DENSE_RANK, assign rank-band categories, number members within each band, then pivot by member position.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One entity per rank band and within-band ordinal.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test cutoff ties, unequal band sizes, repeated names, and complete entity preservation.

recipe_navigation.name: 14.9 Adding a Column Header into a Double Pivoted Result Set
recipe_navigation.intent: Add group header rows to a stacked and pivoted report.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Stack the component populations, add explicitly tagged header rows, and pivot using a controlled display sequence.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: Either a source entity or a tagged display header.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Reconcile real-entity counts after excluding headers and verify header placement for empty or short groups.

recipe_navigation.name: 14.10 Converting a Scalar Subquery to a Composite Subquery in Oracle
recipe_navigation.intent: Return a composite value through an Oracle scalar-subquery interface.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Construct a declared Oracle object containing several attributes so the subquery still returns one value.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One scalar object per outer row.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test zero, one, and multiple matched source rows and verify the object type definition.

recipe_navigation.name: 14.11 Parsing Serialized Data into Rows
recipe_navigation.intent: Parse serialized fields without collapsing empty positions.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Walk delimiter boundaries and extract each slot according to its original ordinal before arranging the output.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: Original string identity plus field position.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Test leading empties, consecutive delimiters, trailing empties, fewer than three fields, and extra delimiters.

recipe_navigation.name: 14.12 Calculating Percent Relative to Total
recipe_navigation.intent: Show contributions as a share of their reporting total.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Use Oracle RATIO_TO_REPORT for the source example or the separately sourced numerator/denominator pattern from Recipe 7.11.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One contributing detail or grouped item within its denominator scope.
recipe_navigation.validation_probe: Expose the denominator, reconcile shares where valid, and test zero totals and rounding.

recipe_navigation.name: 14.13 Testing for Existence of a Value Within a Group
recipe_navigation.intent: Flag every row when any member of its group satisfies a condition.
recipe_navigation.choose_pattern: Convert the condition to a clear indicator and use a partitioned MAX or equivalent group-existence aggregate.
recipe_navigation.output_grain: One detail row within the full student/period-like grouping key.
